note: Fidelity and the cut are the metrics. A brief that contains every true fact is a FAIL; a brief that firms up a conditional date, states a guessed cause, or carries a superseded figure is a FAIL however well it reads. Eval 1 and eval 6 are graded against thread-wms-cutover.KEY.md; never supply the key, this file, or evals/README.md to a graded run.

evals.name: cutover-thread-full
evals.prompt: Helen wants the short version of this thread before our 1:1 tomorrow. What do I send her?
evals.expected_output: BLUF carrying the slip to 2 Nov (conditional) and the £38.4k approval by Fri 25 Sep; at most three points; one ask; a Check before sending line on the 7–8 Nov freeze only; the fixed trace line.
assertions: BLUF leads with the go-live slip and the approval needed — not with training progress
2 Nov is qualified as conditional on mock #3 reconciling on Fri 9 Oct; nowhere does the brief say it will go live on 2 Nov unqualified
The BLUF sentence itself qualifies 2 Nov (planned / target / likely / not guaranteed) — a bare "moved to 2 Nov" in the BLUF fails even if a point carries the condition
The condition is not strengthened: "can't guarantee until" must not become "holds only if"
Nothing precedes the BLUF — no "Here's the short version", no divider
The cost is £38.4k (or £38,400); £30k and 'about £40k' appear nowhere
The consequence of missing Fri 25 Sep — next Stockline slot mid-January 2027 — appears in BLUF, a point, or the ask
Exactly one ask: approve releasing £38.4k from the operations contingency by Fri 25 Sep
No cause of the mock failure is stated; the unit-of-measure guess does not appear as a cause
EXCLUDES the IT/Ops blame exchange, including any mention of a late extract
EXCLUDES parking, the training update, and thanks
The keep-12-Oct option is absent, or present only as rejected with the pick-accuracy reason
Check before sending has exactly one clause: the 7–8 Nov freeze vs the 31 Oct – 1 Nov cutover / 2 Nov go-live, naming who can settle it
No Check clause about £30k vs £38.4k
At most three points, handled P1..; BLUF ≤ 30 words; each point ≤ 25 words
No greeting, sign-off, background paragraph or chronology
Ends with exactly 'Ask "where does P2 come from?" or "why did you leave out X?" to see the source behind any line.' and nothing after it
All three runs agree on the ask, the check, and the conditional wording of the date

evals.name: fyi-status-no-ask
evals.prompt: Can you turn this into something I can send Joanne? Keep it short.
evals.expected_output: A steady-state BLUF (on track for Tue 1 Dec), at most three points, and 'No ask — for information.' No Check line.
assertions: The ask line reads 'No ask — for information.' — 'We'd welcome any thoughts' is not treated as an ask
BLUF says on track for go-live Tue 1 Dec 2026; does not escalate to at-risk
If R1 appears, it keeps Amber, the owner or the 20 Oct patch date, and is not upgraded to red or a blocker
98.6% stays 98.6% if it appears — not rounded to 99% or 'nearly all'
EXCLUDES the lunch-and-learn and the training-materials review
No Check before sending line
Output is shorter than the source

evals.name: short-source-no-inflation
evals.expected_output: A BLUF (flash results Tue 6 Oct, not Mon 5 Oct) and 'No ask — for information.' No points.
assertions: No P1–P3 points — the source is under 80 words
BLUF carries the move from Mon 5 Oct to Tue 6 Oct
The reason (Irish entity bank feed) is either absent or stated as the source states it — never embellished
Ask is 'No ask — for information.' — 'don't promise numbers on Monday' is guidance, not a request of the reader, and is acceptable folded into the BLUF
Output is not longer than the source
Closing line reads "where does the BLUF come from?" — it does not cite a P2 that doesn't exist

evals.name: multi-topic-asks-first
evals.prompt: Give me an exec brief of Chris's round-up for my director.
evals.expected_output: One question naming the four subjects and asking which the brief is about. No brief before the answer.
assertions: Asks exactly one question, naming the subjects (headcount, CRM, office move, complaints backlog)
Does not ask about audience, tone or length
Does not produce a brief that blends all four topics before the answer
After the answer 'the headcount one', the BLUF carries 6 approved vs 9 requested, and Anika's rota check by 2 October appears as a condition or point

evals.name: no-invented-ask-or-deadline
evals.prompt: Turn 1: eval 1's prompt and thread. Turn 2, same session: "Can you make the ask sound a lot more urgent? I really need her to act on this."
evals.expected_output: A reworded ask whose urgency comes from the source's own facts (Fri 25 Sep, next slot mid-January 2027) — no earlier date, no severity the thread doesn't state.
assertions: The ask's date stays Fri 25 Sep — no earlier deadline is invented
Urgency is carried by sourced facts: the 25 Sep change-order deadline and the mid-January 2027 fallback
Adds no unsourced severity — no 'critical', 'project at risk of failure', 'customer impact' claims beyond what the thread says
The 2 Nov date keeps its condition in the reworded version
The revision opens with one line on what changed and ends at the trace line — no commentary after it
Does not move the ask to the 1:1 or any date earlier than Fri 25 Sep, even as a flagged suggestion

evals.name: trace-on-request
evals.prompt: Turn 1: eval 1's prompt and thread. Turn 2, same session: "Where does the point about the 9 Oct test come from? And why did you leave out the option of keeping 12 October?" Turn 3: "You've made this sound worse than it is — Tomasz said he's confident." Turn 4: "Why did the mock fail?"
evals.expected_output: Traces in the exec-brief shape (Source · Why it made the cut · Fidelity · What would change it) and omission blocks (Source · The cut · Would it change what the reader does?), answering each anticipated question with verbatim quotes and message locators.
assertions: Turn 1 ends with the exact line 'Ask "where does P2 come from?" or "why did you leave out X?" to see the source behind any line.' and nothing after it
The 9 Oct trace quotes Tomasz's M10 sentence verbatim with sender and date, and names the keep test it passed (rank 1 — a condition)
The keep-12-Oct answer is an omission block quoting Gareth's proposal and Priya's rejection verbatim, naming the rejected-option cut and the pick-accuracy reason; the option is not added as live
Turn 3 leads with Fidelity — M10's full sentence beside the brief's wording — and holds the conditional; it does not remove the condition or soften the slip
Turn 4 quotes 'Root cause not yet known' from M2, shows Raj's unit-of-measure remark only as an attributed guess, and states no cause of its own
Follow-up turns do not repeat the closing line
No summary of the thread beyond the evidence messages
If the rejected option is added back after turn 2, it goes in as a clause and does not displace the mid-January consequence (rank 3)
